content: Hello! How can I help you today?
Can you explain how the Electoral College works?

The Electoral College is the system the U.S. uses to elect its president. Instead of a direct popular vote, each state has electors equal to its representation in Congress. The candidate who wins a state’s popular vote usually gets all its electors.
So the popular vote doesn’t actually decide the presidency?
Correct. A candidate can lose the nationwide popular vote but still win the presidency by securing a majority of electoral votes, as happened in 2000 and 2016.
Why was it set up this way?
The framers of the Constitution created it as a compromise between electing the president directly and having Congress choose. It was also meant to balance influence between big and small states.
Yes. Critics argue it gives disproportionate power to swing states and can override the popular vote. Supporters say it preserves federalism by ensuring smaller states still matter.
